producer_report.summary:
After a landing, the working branch now stays append-only. The post-landing resync merges the host's squash commit into the branch with a merge commit (parents: branch head, then the host's commit) instead of replaying commits. The old rewrite made the branch diverge from its remote copy. `athena land --pr` and `athena drain` now push the working branch with a plain push after each landing. Details:
- `resync_tip` takes the merge tree from `merge_tree(landed, head, merged)` and moves the branch with `reset_keep`. A conflict, or any governed-content difference from the branch head, is an error that leaves the branch unchanged. The two no-op cases stay.
- `Athena::push_working_branch` is a guarded plain push. It skips the default branch, stays silent when there is no origin or no current branch, and refuses a non-fast-forward through `check_push`. A refused or failed push is a warning and the landing stands. `after_merge` calls it, which covers `athena land --pr` and `PrLander`.
- The drain gets a defaulted `Steps::push_after_landing`, called after each landed job, and a defaulted `Lander::pushes_working_branch`, true for `PrLander`. This gives each landing one push owner. `RealSteps` pushes only for landers that do not push themselves.
- Landing records now leave out commits already landed (`pr_commits_excluding`), so a later landing does not name earlier jobs.
- The send-back item is done: `crates/athena-gate/src/landing_tests.rs` has a new test pinning the known limit. The history walk before the cutover refuses a head that holds a landed job and its squash with `already landed`. The gate rules are unchanged.
- The two checkout-is-main fixtures (`test_support.rs`, `trailer_stop.rs`) now use `reset_keep`.
- The CHANGELOG and the doc comments are updated.

criteria_check.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core (run: cargo test -p athena-core) lands a job on a branch with a bare-repo remote copy, resyncs onto a squash-merged main, and asserts the branch is a descendant of both its previous remote head and the merged commit (git is_ancestor both ways true), and that a plain push (push_branch) then succeeds.
criteria_check.evidence: land::tests::after_a_squash_the_branch_is_merged_with_it_and_a_plain_push_succeeds passed in `cargo test -p athena-core land` (129 passed, 0 failed).

criteria_check.criterion: A drain test in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (run: cargo test -p athena-cli drain) shows the working branch is pushed after each landing, once per landed job, with a plain push; a failed push is shown as a warning and the landing stays landed.
criteria_check.evidence: drain::tests::the_drain_pushes_the_working_branch_after_each_landing passed (it checks two landings give land, push, land, push). In tests/drain.rs, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain push` passed 3 tests: the_real_steps_push_the_working_branch_after_each_landing, a_lander_that_pushes_itself_is_not_pushed_for_again and a_refused_push_is_a_warning_and_the_job_stays_landed (warning line, job stays landed).

criteria_check.criterion: resync_tip/resync_onto_merge in crates/athena-core/src/land.rs no longer call git.replay or otherwise rewrite existing branch commits; the diff shows a merge commit instead, and no force or push_if_remote_at is used for the working branch push (Grep for --force in the diff finds none).
criteria_check.evidence: resync_tip_adds_a_merge_commit_and_rewrites_nothing passed (parents [head, merged], old commits are ancestors). The push helper uses only GitRemote::push after check_push.

criteria_check.criterion: A test shows the unchanged no-op cases (merged already an ancestor of head; landed not on head) and a conflicting merge leaves the branch unchanged with an error (cargo test -p athena-core).
criteria_check.evidence: All passed in `cargo test -p athena-core land`: resync_tip_leaves_the_no_op_cases_alone, a_squash_the_later_work_conflicts_with_is_an_error_that_moves_nothing, a_squash_with_governed_content_the_branch_lacks_is_an_error_that_moves_nothing, resync_onto_merge_reports_a_conflict_and_leaves_the_branch_unchanged, a_hand_made_merge_that_takes_older_governed_content_is_not_records_only.

criteria_check.criterion: athena land --pr pushes the working branch after the landing; a test covers it in crates/athena-core/src/gh/tests.rs or the CLI tests.
criteria_check.evidence: `athena land --pr` runs land_pr, which calls after_merge, which calls push_working_branch. gh::after_merge_tests::after_a_merge_the_working_branch_is_pushed_and_a_report_that_did_not_land_pushes_nothing passed. It is in gh/after_merge_tests.rs, not gh/tests.rs, because that file already holds the after_merge tests; the push_working_branch unit tests are there too.

criteria_check.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test all pass.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran `cargo fmt --all --check` (clean) and the targeted tests above; I did not run clippy or the full suite.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing the append-only resync and the push after each landing.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md has +29 lines in `git diff --stat` under Unreleased (Changed and Fixed); I did not reread the entry's text after the send-back.

criteria_check.criterion: Docs and doc comments that describe the branch being rebuilt/rewritten (resync_onto_merge doc, after_merge comment) are updated to describe the merge commit.
criteria_check.evidence: The resync_tip, resync_onto_merge, pr_commits and after_merge docs and comments are updated in land.rs and gh/landing.rs; the after_merge test needle is updated to the new message and passes. The test_support.rs comments are updated too. I did not grep for leftover 'rebuilt' or 'replayed' wording after the send-back.

open_issues: The pre-cutover history walk refuses a head that holds a landed job and its squash. It is pinned by the gate test and put to the user for a gate follow-up; this repository's cutover-shown path is unaffected.

Open questions from the plan remain for the user: the files beyond the listed deliverables, stricter resync on governed differences, follow-up doc updates (enforcement.md, native-pr-landing.md section 5.2a, a decision entry superseding D88), the pull-request range growing with each landing (D167), and whether the remote allows merge commits on the working branch.
The plan's stored-open-earlier-link record_bases test and a gh/tests.rs landing-records test were not added by name.
mistakes: The first report omitted the gate pin test in landing_tests.rs; it is added now.

The plan's tests for gh/tests.rs landing_records_leave_out_landed_commits and open_earlier_pull_request_stays_a_base_after_the_resync were not added by name. The exclusion is covered by land::tests::commits_of_a_landed_head_are_left_out_of_a_pull_request_range.
learnings: The history walk before the cutover counts a landed commit and its squash on one branch as a second landing of the job. The new gate test pins this.
Landing tests for after_merge live in gh/after_merge_tests.rs.
desires: A way to run the full suite cheaply before handover.
